hook_text: The water in one river can grow food, make electricity, help mine gold and still have room for a swim.
clip_script: The Vaal River on a summer's day. Sailboats glide across the Vaal Dam. Downstream, a power station uses river water to make steam and electricity. A factory pumps water in to make fuel and plastics. Further on, gold mines need water to work. And far to the south-west, canals carry Vaal water to green fields of maize, wheat and pecan nuts. One river, many jobs. Without water, none of it would work.
visual_style: Whiteboard river winding across the page, with labelled stops: a dam with a sailboat, a power station with cooling towers, a factory, a mine headgear and green irrigated fields.
mood: Busy and amazed, like discovering how much one thing can do.
pacing: Float downstream from stop to stop, one use of water at each.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find something in your home that needed water to make.
